verses.text: After a long time, in the third year, the LORD told Elijah, “Go present yourself to Ahab, and I'll send rain on the land.”
So Elijah went to see Ahab. By then the famine in Samaria was severe.
Ahab summoned Obadiah, who managed his household. Obadiah had great reverence for the LORD.
When Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets, Obadiah had taken a hundred of them and hidden them in two caves, fifty in each. He supplied them with bread and water.
Ahab told Obadiah, “Go through the land and check every spring and stream. Maybe we'll find enough grass to keep the horses and mules alive so we don't lose all our animals.”
They divided the land between them to search it. Ahab went one way on his own, and Obadiah went another way on his own.
As Obadiah was on the road, Elijah met him. Obadiah recognized him, fell facedown, and said, “Is it really you, my lord Elijah?”
“Yes, it's me,” Elijah said. “Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”
Obadiah replied, “What wrong have I done that you'd hand me over to Ahab to be killed?

As surely as the LORD your God lives, there's no nation or kingdom my master hasn't sent people to search for you. When they said, ‘He isn't here,’ he made the nation or kingdom swear they hadn't found you.
And now you're telling me to go to my master and say, ‘Elijah is here!’

As soon as I leave you, the LORD's Spirit could carry you somewhere I don't know. Then I'll tell Ahab, he'll come looking for you, and when he can't find you he'll kill me. I've honored the LORD since I was young.
Haven't you heard what I did when Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets? I hid a hundred of them, fifty to a cave, and gave them bread and water.
Now you want me to tell my master, ‘Elijah is here.’ He'll kill me!”
Elijah answered, “As surely as the LORD of Armies, whom I serve, lives, I'll present myself to Ahab today.”
So Obadiah went to Ahab and told him. Then Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw him, he asked, “Is that you, the one who's been making trouble for Israel?”
Elijah answered, “I haven't made trouble for Israel. You and your father's family did that when you abandoned the LORD's commands and went after the Baals.
Now send word and gather all Israel to meet me at Mount Carmel. Bring the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table.”
So Ahab sent word throughout Israel and gathered the prophets on Mount Carmel.
Elijah stepped forward and asked the people, “How long will you keep going back and forth between two sides? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is, follow him.” Nobody said a word.
Then Elijah told the people, “I'm the only prophet of the LORD left here, and Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.
Bring us two bulls. Let them choose one, cut it up, and lay it on the wood without lighting a fire. I'll prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood without lighting a fire either.
Call on the name of your god, and I'll call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers with fire is God.” All the people said, “That's fair.”
Elijah told Baal's prophets, “Choose a bull and prepare yours first, since there are so many of you. Call on your god's name, but don't light the fire.”
They prepared the bull they'd been given and called on Baal from morning until noon. “Baal, answer us!” they shouted. There was no voice and nobody answered. They jumped around the altar they'd made.
At noon Elijah began mocking them. “Shout louder! He's a god, after all. Maybe he's lost in thought, stepped away, or gone on a trip. Maybe he's asleep and somebody needs to wake him.”
They shouted louder and cut themselves with knives and spears as their custom was, until blood poured out.
They kept prophesying past midday until the time of the evening offering. There was no voice, no answer, and nobody paid attention.
Then Elijah told everyone, “Come closer.” They gathered around him, and he repaired the LORD's altar, which had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe descended from Jacob, the man the LORD had told, “Your name will be Israel.”
He built an altar with the stones in the LORD's name. He dug a trench around it large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
He arranged the wood, cut up the bull, and laid it on the wood. Then he said, “Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and the wood.”
“Do it again,” he said, and they did. “Do it a third time,” he said, and they did it a third time.
Water ran down around the altar, and the trench filled with water too.

At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet stepped forward and prayed, “LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let everyone know today that you are God in Israel, I am your servant, and I've done all this at your word.
Answer me, LORD, answer me so these people will know that you are God and that you've turned their hearts back to you.”
The LORD's fire fell and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust. It licked up the water in the trench.
When the people saw it, they fell facedown and cried, “The LORD is God! The LORD is God!”
Elijah told them, “Seize Baal's prophets! Don't let any escape!” They seized them, and Elijah took them down to the Kishon stream and killed them there.
Then Elijah told Ahab, “Go on up and eat and drink. I hear the sound of heavy rain.”
Ahab went up to eat and drink, while Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel, bent low to the ground, and put his face between his knees.
He told his servant, “Go up and look toward the sea.” The servant looked and said, “There's nothing.” Elijah kept telling him to go back, seven times in all.

The seventh time the servant reported, “A small cloud the size of a man's hand is coming up out of the sea.” Elijah told him, “Go tell Ahab, ‘Get your chariot ready and head down before the rain stops you.’”
Soon the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and heavy rain poured down. Ahab rode toward Jezreel.
The LORD's hand was on Elijah. He tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab to the entrance to Jezreel.
